summary.text: 饿 means “hungry.” It is the simplified form of 餓: the food-related component 食 appears in its simplified left-side form 饣, while 我 provides the sound cue in the traditional analysis.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: in 餓, 食 marks the food-related meaning and 我 supplies a sound cue. 饿 is the simplified character form of 餓, with 食 written as 饣; this is a graphic standardization, not a separate ancient construction.

components.text: In traditional 餓, 食 is the semantic component, associating the character with food and hunger. In simplified 饿, its corresponding left-side form is 饣; the two are full and positional simplified forms, not evidence of a historical sequence.
我 is the phonetic component in 餓. The Zhengzhang reconstructions *ŋaːlʔ for 我 and *ŋaːls for 餓 share a segmental base but differ in ending. Their Mandarin readings, wǒ and è, are not identical today.

sound.text: Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison: 我 *ŋaːlʔ and 餓 *ŋaːls share the segmental base, despite differing endings. These are reconstructions, not recorded pronunciations.

history.text: The traditional 餓 is analyzed as 食 on the left and 我 on the right. The Shuowen account gives this component analysis, and a modern regular-script description also places 食 left and 我 right. A Qin-slip specimen and a transmitted ancient form are reported in reference lists, but their glyph images were not inspected, so they do not establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.
饿 is the simplified form of 餓, with 食 represented by its simplified left-side form 饣. This describes a standardization between character forms; it does not show that 饣 preceded 食 historically.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not establish an exact earliest attestation or a complete early graphic sequence for 餓. A reported Qin-slip specimen has not been visually checked, and no secure oracle-bone or bronze form was established in the research.

The object originally depicted by 我 is disputed, and its proposed original name and pronunciation remain unrecovered here. That uncertainty does not remove the separately supported phonetic role of 我 in 餓.

senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 餓 as 飢, “hungry.” Literary examples are reported for the intransitive sense “be hungry,” but the cited works are not dated in this evidence, so this is the earliest supported sense in the dossier, not a claim about first-ever use.

senses.period: some early literary usage; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Dictionary reports of Huainanzi and Han Feizi passages describe some usage distinguishing 餓 from 飢 by degree, with 餓 for more severe hunger. This reported contrast should not be treated as the only historical distinction or as a precisely dated stage.

senses.gloss: make hungry; cause to suffer hunger
senses.text: A Mencius citation is reported for a causative use meaning “make hungry.” The evidence records this use but does not establish when it arose relative to the intransitive hunger sense.

senses.gloss: poor; lacking, including lack of water
senses.period: later dialectal usage; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Later dialect examples are reported with meanings such as “poor” or “lacking,” including water-starved fields. The evidence does not establish when this sense arose or a precise semantic path from hunger to lack.
“Greedy for” appears among the supplied modern glosses, but this evidence does not establish its chronology or relation to the hunger sense.

developments.text: Some reported early usage distinguishes 餓 as more severe hunger than 飢; this is a limited usage distinction, not a complete account of the character’s meanings.

limitations.text: The classical citations and reported manuscript citation do not provide dates sufficient to establish the first attestation or a full chronology of these senses.
The available evidence does not establish the semantic development connecting hunger to “poor” or “lacking,” or the chronology of that extension.
The listed modern gloss “greedy for” has no dated or otherwise supported semantic history in this dossier.

overview.text: 饿 means “hungry.” In traditional 餓, 食 connects the character with food and 我 supplies a sound cue. 饿 is the simplified form of 餓, with 食 written as 饣.

components.text: 饣 is the simplified left-side form corresponding to 食, the food-related component in traditional 餓.
我 provides the sound cue in traditional 餓. Its original pictured object and name remain uncertain, but that does not affect this role.

relationships.text: 饣 is the simplified left-side form corresponding to 食, which supplies the food-related semantic category in 饿’s traditional form.
饿 is the simplified form of 餓; 食 is represented by its simplified positional form 饣.
In the traditional graph 餓, 食 supplies the food-related semantic category.
我 supplies the sound cue in 餓, supported by the same-system Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison.
